Practical Restoration Guidance

Clothing & Textile Restoration FAQs

Straightforward answers about fire, smoke, soot, water and flood-affected clothing and textiles. Every item requires an individual assessment.

Can smoke odors be removed from clothing?

Some smoke-affected clothing may be suitable for professional textile care. Results depend on fabric construction, the kind and extent of exposure, and the condition of the item. An inspection is needed; complete odor removal cannot be promised.

Can soot-damaged clothing be restored?

Soot can settle on surfaces, seams and linings. Some garments may be recoverable, but heat, residues, dyes and fabric condition all matter. Avoid rubbing soot into textiles or using harsh cleaning products before seeking guidance.

What should I do with wet clothing after a leak or flood?

Keep affected textiles separate from dry, unaffected items where practical, and avoid leaving wet items sealed in bags. Water from sewage or flooding may contain hazardous contamination. Follow property safety guidance before handling exposed belongings.

Can wedding gowns, quilts and specialty garments be evaluated?

These items may require individual evaluation because lace, layers, stitching, dyes and finishes react differently. ACR's Results gallery includes original job photographs of a wedding gown and quilt; photographs cannot establish the suitability of another item.

How do I know if clothing can be saved?

The source of damage, fabric, heat exposure, staining, contamination and overall condition help determine what can reasonably be restored. Not every item is recoverable. Call ACR to discuss the affected textiles and next steps.

How long will restoration take, and how much will it cost?

Time and cost depend on the number and type of articles, their condition and the work required. The website does not publish a fixed turnaround time or standard quote. Contact ACR for information about your specific situation.

How do I contact ACR about affected belongings?

Call 717-738-2679. It may help to describe whether the damage involved fire, smoke, soot or water, which textiles are involved, and any known contamination or heat exposure. ACR is based at 17A East Queen Street, Ephrata, Pennsylvania 17522.
